raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I've been doing wheat and maize on these 3 mu for a long time, so I pretty much know what to expect.

**Wheat first — going in this October**

I'll plant around October 10-15, same as always. The extension station told us a few years back to aim for mid-October because the weather's been warmer lately, and if you plant too early the wheat grows too tall before winter and then the cold hurts it. I usually buy seed from the agricultural supply shop in town — Jimai 22 or whatever they have that year, a semi-improved variety. I don't save seed anymore because the yield gets worse after a couple years. Seed costs maybe 8 yuan per mu.

For fertilizer, I put down a compound fertilizer (15-15-15 or similar) before planting — about one and a half bags per mu, that's roughly 75 kg of compound, which gives me about 11 kg of N, 11 of P, 11 of K as the base. Then at jointing in March or April, if the wheat looks a bit yellow or thin, I topdress urea — maybe 15 kg per mu, so another 7 kg of N. Total N comes out around 18 kg/mu. I know the extension guy said 15 is enough but I usually do a bit more because I'd rather waste a little fertilizer than lose yield. With only 3 mu, I can't afford a bad harvest.

Irrigation — I pump from the well 3 times for wheat: once before winter to get it through the cold (around late November), once at green-up/jointing (March), and once at grain filling (May) if it hasn't rained. Pumping costs money — electricity and the fee — so I don't do more than that. If the rain comes at the right time I might skip one.

Pesticide — I'll spray herbicide once in spring for weeds (that's almost automatic now, the weeds are terrible otherwise), and I watch for aphids at heading. If I see them, I spray; if not, I don't.

Yield I'm hoping for 450 kg/mu. Last year I got about 430. My neighbor on better soil gets 500 but his field is in a lower spot.

**Maize after wheat — mid-June**

The turnaround is tight. As soon as the wheat combine comes through in early-mid June, I need to get the maize in the ground within a few days. I hire the neighbor with the no-till planter — costs about 30 yuan/mu but it's the only way to get it in fast enough. Straw stays on the ground as mulch.

I plant a hybrid — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has. Seed's around 25-30 yuan/mu for hybrid.

Fertilizer for maize: I apply compound at planting with the planter, maybe 40 kg/mu of a high-N compound, then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage (around late July) — about 20 kg/mu of urea. That puts total N around 16-17 kg/mu.

Irrigation — usually the summer rains handle most of it. But if July is dry I'll pump once or twice. Figure 1-2 times.

Pesticide — herbicide at planting for sure. Maybe insecticide for armyworms if I see them.

Yield target 500 kg/mu. Got 480 last year.

**The money side**

It's just me and my wife on 3 mu. No hired labor except the planter operator and the combine operators. Our son works in the city, sends money home, so we're not desperate but we don't waste either. Total input cost for both crops will be around 500-600 yuan per mu per season, so maybe 3,500 yuan for the year across both crops on all 3 mu.
